newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares make further gains.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares make further gains.

text.p: Nigerian equities made further gains on sustained demand in Wednesday trading, dealers said.
The all-share index closed at 6469.97 from 6,422.93 on Tuesday.
"The gains were fuelled by investors' growing appetite for equities rather than any new information," one trader said.
Union Bank closed 35 kobo higher at 8.05 naira. Guaranty Trust Bank, listed last week, rose 25 kobo to 13.00 naira. FSB International Bank closed 17 kobo higher at 5.00 naira.
Cement shares maintained a strong performance. West African Portland Cement gained 50 kobo to 31.70 naira, while Ashaka Cement closed 38 kobo higher at 16.50 naira.

Construction company Cappa and D'Alberto rose 37 kobo, or five percent to close at 7.76 naira. Cadbury and Nigerian Bottling Company gained 50 kobo apiece to close at 26.00 naira and 28.50 naira respectively.
AIICO Insurance closed 25 kobo higher at 6.40 naira. Evans Medical added 10 kobo to 2.80 naira. Pharma-Deko rose five kobo to 3.40 naira; Pfizer Products, 10 kobo to 7.30 naira.
African Petroleum led oil marketing companies, up 70 kobo at 30.20 naira. Unipetrol ended 40 kobo higher at 38.70 naira. National Oil finished 33 kobo higher at 30.33 naira.

In the conglomerates sector the biggest loser was UAC, which fell 20 kobo to 11.05 naira on poorly received half-year results announced on Wednesday. CFAO shares were 10 kobo down at 4.40 naira. SCOA fell one kobo to finish at 2.33 naira.
Guinness was the only brewer to lose, dropping 10 kobo to 8.95 naira. Carnaud Metal Box slid five kobo lower at 4.10 naira while Studio Press ended four kobo lower at 1.10 naira.
